PaperCopper(I) Iodide Mediated Synthesis of Carbohydrate-Based Terminal 
Allenes by ATA Reaction
Carbohydrate-Based Terminal Allenes
Xin Huang, Chunling Fu, Shengming Ma*
Laboratory of Molecular Recognition and Synthesis, Department of Chemistry, Zhejiang University, 310027 Hangzhou, Zhejiang, P. R. of China
Fax +86(21)62609305; E-mail: masm@sioc.ac.cn
Received: 27.05.2014; Accepted after revision: 20.06.2014
Abstract: We have demonstrated two improved methods for the
synthesis of carbohydrate-based terminal allenes from propargyl or
homopropargyl glycosides. The reaction of propargyl or homoprop-
argyl glycosides with paraformaldehyde (2.5 equiv) in the presence
of copper(I) iodide (10 mol%) and diisopropylamine (1.8 equiv) or
copper(I) iodide (50 mol%) and dicyclohexylamine (1.8 equiv) pro-
duces sugar-linked terminal allenes in 50–79% yield.
Key words: copper(I) iodide, diisopropy lamine, dicyclohexyl-
amine, carbohydrates, allenes
Carbohydrate chemistry has become more and more im-
portant, since carbohydrates exist widely in natural prod-
ucts with remarkable biological activities. 1 However,
there are limited reports 2 on allenes with carbohydrate
moieties. Sugar-linked 1,2-allenyl ethers are usually pre-
pared by the isomerization of propargyl glycosides in the
presence of a strong base.
2a–c During the past few decades,
allene chemistry has experienced great progress, since al-
lenes are very useful intermediates in organic synthesis.
3
About 150 natural products containing an allenic or cumu-
lenic structure have been found, and this turned out to be
a very attractive and prolific area of interest.4 So far, dif-
ferent kinds of synthetic methods to produce functional al-
lenes
5 have been developed, among which the allenylation
of terminal alkynes (ATA reaction) with paraformalde-
hyde [(HCHO)
n] in the presence of amines and copper(I)
salts may be the most straigh tforward method to obtain
terminal allenes.6 Although many functional groups such
as mesylate, ether, hydroxy, amide, and so forth are toler-
ated under the current conditions, it is still interesting to
introduce this method for the synthesis of more complicat-
ed carbohydrate-based allenes, since some functionalities
are not well tolerated under the original protocol.
7 In this
paper, we wish to report an easy application of copper(I)
iodide mediated synthesis of carbohydrate-based terminal
allenes from propargyl or homopropargyl glycosides
(Scheme 1).
Initially, we chose prop-2-ynyl-substituted 2,3,4,6-tetra-
O-acetyl-β-

6a or diisopropylamine with

To our delight, when 50 mol% copper(I) iodide was used,

cyclohexylamine
6d seems to be slightly better than diiso-
propylamine with copper(I) io dide (50 mol%), affording
2a in 73% yield (entry 6). Thus, we defined the combina-
tion of copper(I) iodide (10 mol%) and diisopropylamine
(1.8 equiv) as standard conditions A and the combination
of copper(I) iodide (50 mol% ) and dicyclohexylamine
(1.8 equiv) as standard conditions B.

proved methods of allenylation of terminal alkynes devel-
